groups.description: How a release reaches the people who install it.
What a release proves about where it came from.
Which setups a release promises to keep working.

data.title: Publish release candidates to the main channel?
data.case: Situation: users run tidy upgrade and pick up whatever the latest tag is. Now: a release candidate goes to the next channel only, with npm publish --access public --provenance --tag next && gh release create v2.4.0-rc.1 --prerelease --generate-notes --verify-tag. Alternative: publish it as latest, as pip does for pre-releases when asked with --pre, so more people test it. Recommendation: keep the separate channel; a broken candidate would reach everyone.

data.title: Ship a single static binary next to the package?
data.case: Situation: the package needs Node 20 on the machine. Now: nobody gets a binary. Alternative: build one per platform with bun build --compile --target=bun-linux-x64 --outfile dist/tidy-linux-x64 src/cli.ts, as ripgrep and fd do. Recommendation: yes, for Linux and macOS first; it removes the Node requirement for CI users.

data.title: Keep a changelog file in the repository?
data.case: Situation: release notes are written by the release tool from merged pull requests. Now: there is no CHANGELOG.md; notes live on the release page. Alternative: also commit them, as most libraries do, so they travel with a clone. Recommendation: generate the file at release time; no extra writing.

data.title: Sign release archives with a project key?
data.case: Situation: anyone can download the archive from the release page. Now: archives are unsigned and checked only by a checksum file next to them. Alternative: sign with cosign sign-blob --yes --output-signature tidy.tar.gz.sig --output-certificate tidy.tar.gz.pem tidy.tar.gz, which Go and Kubernetes releases do. Recommendation: yes; a checksum on the same page proves nothing if the page is altered.

data.title: Require two reviewers for changes to the release workflow?
data.case: Situation: the workflow holds the publishing token. Now: one reviewer can approve a change to it. Alternative: a code-owners rule that asks two, as most registries recommend for publishing code. Recommendation: yes; it slows a change to this one file only.

data.title: Pin third-party actions to commit hashes?
data.case: Situation: the workflow uses six actions from other authors. Now: they are pinned to tags, which their authors can move. Alternative: pin to hashes and let a bot propose updates. Recommendation: yes, with the bot, so pinning does not freeze fixes.

data.title: Drop Node 18 in this release?
data.case: Situation: Node 18 reached end of life in April. Now: the package still runs on it, and CI tests it. Alternative: require Node 20 and say so in the release notes, as the other tools in this space already did. Recommendation: drop it; the tests on 18 take a third of the CI time.

data.title: Keep the old --legacy-paths flag for another release?
data.case: Situation: the flag was deprecated in 2.2 and prints a warning. Now: it still works. Alternative: remove it, which the 2.2 notes promised for 2.4. Recommendation: remove it as promised; point to tidy migrate-paths in the error.

data.title: Support Windows paths with spaces in the config file?
data.case: Situation: three users reported C:\Program Files\Tidy\tidy.toml failing to load. Now: such paths fail with an unreadable error. Alternative: quote-aware parsing, which costs one day and a new test matrix entry. Recommendation: fix it; it is the most reported problem this quarter.

data.title: Publish the type definitions as a separate package?
data.case: Situation: the types ship inside the main package. Now: they follow its version. Alternative: split them out, as DefinitelyTyped does, so they can be fixed without a release. Recommendation: no; one version is simpler for everyone.
